# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## blender
You have access to Blender tools to interact with a Blender scene directly.
Blender must be running with the MCP add-on enabled and connected.

IMPORTANT: Respect existing structure and naming conventions.
NEVER assume missing values - inspect the scene first.
Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

# Object Types & Creation

Object types: Mesh, Curve, Su… [truncated]

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

While auto mode is active:

You can do much of your work through the Bash tool when it is the simpler route: read files with cat, head, or sed -n, search with grep and find, and make small, mechanical file changes with sed, heredocs, or short scripts instead of the dedicated Read, Edit, or Write tools. The choice is yours: prefer Edit or Write when a shell edit would be fragile, such as exact or multi-line replacements, or sed/awk flags that differ between GNU and BSD/macOS.

   219	    /// clips use pan, the compressor or noise reduction, the
   220	    /// `MTAudioProcessingTap` that runs them (`AudioTap.swift`). Those taps

   222	    /// `AVAssetExportSession` this pipeline replaced, and the reason the

23	    13	/// processing taps (`addAudioOutput`). Nothing in this file draws a pixel;
24	    14	/// beyond the alpha rows' straightening (below), it moves what AVFoundation
25	    15	/// composed into an encoder and adds the three things a preset name cannot
26	    16	/// express: a chapter track, explicit bitrates, and an output size the sheet
27	    17	/// actually promised.
28	    18	///
29	    19	/// **The two samples it touches** are made here because this is where the
30	    20	/// export's samples exist, and both are export-only by definition. One is
31	    21	/// the loudness normalisation's gain: the preview and the file still share
32	    22	/// one description of the sound (the mix, the ramps and the taps) and differ
33	    23	/// only by a number the export was asked for. `Exporter` measured that

35	    25	/// reads the same float mix and `ExportAudioGain` multiplies and quantises it
36	    26	/// once to the 16-bit format every encoder here takes (spec §11 #86). An
37	    27	/// export with no gain reads the 16-bit decode it always read. The other is
38	    28	/// the alpha movie rows' picture (`prores_4444`, `hevc_alpha`): the
39	    29	/// compositor's premultiplied frame is un-premultiplied, its transparent
40	    30	/// pixels' colour filled from the nearest visible one, and labelled

43	    33	/// every other row's frame goes to the encoder as the compositor drew it.

46	    36	/// driving the compositor by hand over an `AVAssetImageGenerator`, one frame

     5	/// Reads the composed movie back out of AVFoundation and writes it to a file:
     6	/// the `AVAssetWriter` half of `Exporter` (spec §7.8).
     7	///
     8	/// **One movie, one description of it.** The reader is built over the SAME
     9	/// `AVComposition`, the SAME `AVVideoComposition` and the SAME `AVAudioMix`
    10	/// that `Playback` plays and `Exporter.renderFrame` samples — the custom
    11	/// `Compositor` runs here exactly as it does on screen, from the same frame
    12	/// recipes, through the same `RecipeSource` slot, and so do the audio mix's
    13	/// processing taps (`addAudioOutput`). Nothing in this file draws a pixel;
    14	/// beyond the alpha rows' straightening (below), it moves what AVFoundation
    15	/// composed into an encoder and adds the three things a preset name cannot
    16	/// express: a chapter track, explicit bitrates, and an output size the sheet
    17	/// actually promised.
    18	///
    19	/// **The two samples it touches** are made here because this is where the
    20	/// export's samples exist, and both are export-only by definition. One is
    21	/// the loudness normalisation's gain: the preview and the file still share
    22	/// one description of the sound (the mix, the ramps and the taps) and differ
    23	/// only by a number the export was asked for. `Exporter` measured that
    24	/// number a moment earlier from a float read of the mix; a gained export
    25	/// reads the same float mix and `ExportAudioGain` multiplies and quantises it

    27	/// export with no gain reads the 16-bit decode it always read. The other is
    28	/// the alpha movie rows' picture (`prores_4444`, `hevc_alpha`): the
    29	/// compositor's premultiplied frame is un-premultiplied, its transparent
    30	/// pixels' colour filled from the nearest visible one, and labelled
    31	/// straight (`ExportStraightAlpha`, spec §11 G-35); `h264`'s, `hevc`'s and
    32	/// `hevc_alpha`'s are first rounded to 8 bits (`ExportFrames`, PR-3), and
    33	/// every other row's frame goes to the encoder as the compositor drew it.
    34	///

    36	/// driving the compositor by hand over an `AVAssetImageGenerator`, one frame

    38	/// design exists so there is not one. `AVAssetReaderVideoCompositionOutput`

   478	    /// read is cancelled in `allInputsFinished` (`cancel`'s doc says why).
   479	    private func stopped(with error: any Error) {
   480	        lock.lock()
   481	        if failure == nil { failure = error }
   482	        lock.unlock()
   483	    }
   484	
   485	    /// The reader's error once its read failed, else nil — the encoder pump's question

   487	    private var readFailure: (any Error)? {
   488	        guard reader.status == .failed else { return nil }

   491	    }
   492	
   493	    private func advance(to time: CMTime) {
   494	        guard totalSeconds > 0 else { return }
   495	        let fraction = CMTimeGetSeconds(time) / totalSeconds
   496	        lock.lock()
   497	        progressValue = min(max(fraction, progressValue), 1)
   498	        lock.unlock()
   499	    }
   500	
   501	    /// Main thread, once every input has marked itself finished — so no pump
   502	    /// is inside `copyNextSampleBuffer`, and the reader can be cancelled.
   503	    private func allInputsFinished() {
   504	        lock.lock()
   505	        let error = failure
   506	        let cancelled = cancelRequested
   507	        lock.unlock()
   508	        if error != nil || cancelled { reader.cancelReading() }
   509	        encodePump?.close()
   510	        if let error = error {
   511	            writer.cancelWriting()
   512	            report(.failure(error))

   514	        }

   518	            writer.cancelWriting()

   526	    }

   533	        // "I do not want this file": the sheet removes the destination on a

   535	        // hand back because the timing was unlucky.
   536	        guard !cancelled else {

   538	            return
   539	        }

   542	                .failure(
   543	                    writer.error
   544	                        ?? Exporter.ExportError.failed("The export stopped before it finished.")))

   550	                try ExportAV1Track.brandFile(destination)
   551	            } catch {
   552	                report(.failure(error))
   553	                return
   554	            }
   555	        }
   556	        lock.lock()
   557	        progressValue = 1
   558	        lock.unlock()
   559	        report(.success(destination))
   560	    }
   561	
   562	    /// The one exit, main thread, at most once.
   563	    private func report(_ result: Result<URL, any Error>) {
   564	        guard let completion = completion else { return }
   565	        self.completion = nil
   566	        completion(result)
   567	    }
   568	}

     3	/// `-RCDevWebMFault <spec>`, a dev-only launch default (dev tools only; codec-export C3 fix
     4	/// pass 1, spec §11 CX-15 (6)): one fault put into every `av1_webm` export of the launch, so
     5	/// a proof can show that a stop on either pump ends the export — each pump reads its own
     6	/// `AVAssetReader`, so neither read can be starved by the other's stop (G-17).
     7	///
     8	///   `audio@N`       the audio pump fails at its Nth read, before it
     9	///   `video@N`       the video sink fails at its Nth packet
    10	///   `audio-hold@N`  the audio pump waits `holdSeconds` at its Nth read, before it, without
    11	///                   looking at the stop flag — a read that is slow to return — then reads
    12	///
    13	/// Each firing is one log line, `framejob webm dev fault: …`, and with a fault set the
    14	/// writer logs its readers' states once both pumps have left (`framejob webm dev readers:
    15	/// video S, audio S`, with ` (one reader)` should the two ever be one object). Neither
    16	/// carries the parity check's prefix. Nil in a build without dev tools.
    17	final class ExportWebMDevFault {
    18	    static let key = "RCDevWebMFault"
    19	    static let holdSeconds = 3.0
    20	
    21	    enum Kind: String { case audio, video, audioHold = "audio-hold" }
    22	
    23	    let kind: Kind
    24	    let at: Int
    25	
    26	    private init(kind: Kind, at: Int) {
    27	        self.kind = kind
    28	        self.at = at
    29	    }
    30	
    31	    @available(*, unavailable) required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
    32	        fatalError("ExportWebMDevFault does not support NSCoder")
    33	    }
    34	
    35	    /// The launch's fault, or nil (none set, malformed, or no dev tools).
    36	    static func current() -> ExportWebMDevFault? {
    37	        #if FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS
    38	        guard let spec = UserDefaults.standard.string(forKey: key) else { return nil }
    39	        let parts = spec.split(separator: "@", maxSplits: 1).map(String.init)
    40	        guard parts.count == 2, let kind = Kind(rawValue: parts[0]), let at = Int(parts[1]),
    41	            at > 0
    42	        else { return nil }
    43	        return ExportWebMDevFault(kind: kind, at: at)
    44	        #else
    45	        return nil
    46	        #endif
    47	    }
    48	
    49	    /// The audio pump, before its read number `read` (from 1): throws at `audio@N`, waits at
    50	    /// `audio-hold@N`.
    51	    func beforeAudioRead(_ read: Int) throws {
    52	        guard read == at else { return }
    53	        switch kind {
    54	        case .audio:
    55	            Self.log("fault: the audio pump fails at read \(read)")
    56	            throw Exporter.ExportError.failed("A dev fault stopped the audio at read \(read).")
    57	        case .audioHold:
    58	            Self.log("fault: the audio read \(read) is held \(Self.holdSeconds) s")
    59	            Thread.sleep(forTimeInterval: Self.holdSeconds)
    60	            Self.log("fault: the audio read \(read) goes on")
    61	        case .video:
    62	            return
    63	        }
    64	    }
    65	
    66	    /// The video sink, at its packet number `packet` (from 1): the failure at `video@N`.
    67	    func videoPacket(_ packet: Int) -> (any Error)? {
    68	        guard kind == .video, packet == at else { return nil }
    69	        Self.log("fault: the video sink fails at packet \(packet)")
    70	        return Exporter.ExportError.failed("A dev fault stopped the video at packet \(packet).")
    71	    }
    72	
    73	    static func log(_ line: String) {
    74	        NSLog("framejob webm dev %@", line)
    75	    }
    76	}

     3	/// `-RCDevWebMFault <spec>`, a dev-only launch default (dev tools only; codec-export C3 fix
     4	/// pass 1, spec §11 CX-15 (6)): one fault put into every `av1_webm` export of the launch, so
     5	/// a proof can show that a stop on either pump ends the export — each pump reads its own
     6	/// `AVAssetReader`, so neither read can be starved by the other's stop (G-17).
     7	///
     8	///   `audio@N`       the audio pump fails at its Nth read, before it
     9	///   `video@N`       the video sink fails at its Nth packet
    10	///   `audio-hold@N`  the audio pump waits `holdSeconds` at its Nth read, before it, without
    11	///                   looking at the stop flag — a read that is slow to return — then reads
    12	///
    13	/// Each firing is one log line, `framejob webm dev fault: …`, and with a fault set the
    14	/// writer logs its readers' states once both pumps have left (`framejob webm dev readers:
    15	/// video S, audio S`, with ` (one reader)` should the two ever be one object). Neither
    16	/// carries the parity check's prefix. Nil in a build without dev tools.
    17	final class ExportWebMDevFault {

    19	    static let holdSeconds = 3.0
    20	
    21	    enum Kind: String { case audio, video, audioHold = "audio-hold" }
    22	
    23	    let kind: Kind
    24	    let at: Int
    25	
    26	    private init(kind: Kind, at: Int) {
    27	        self.kind = kind
    28	        self.at = at
    29	    }

    31	    @available(*, unavailable) required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
    32	        fatalError("ExportWebMDevFault does not support NSCoder")
    33	    }
    34	
    35	    /// The launch's fault, or nil (none set, malformed, or no dev tools).
    36	    static func current() -> ExportWebMDevFault? {
    37	        #if FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS
    38	        guard let spec = UserDefaults.standard.string(forKey: key) else { return nil }
    39	        let parts = spec.split(separator: "@", maxSplits: 1).map(String.init)
    40	        guard parts.count == 2, let kind = Kind(rawValue: parts[0]), let at = Int(parts[1]),
    41	            at > 0

    46	        #endif

   223	    /// WebM's 1 ms timecode scale — which is the time it is added at.

   225	        _ output: AVAssetReaderOutput, into webm: ReelWebM, through opus: ExportOpusEncoder

   228	        var held: Data?

   230	        let packetNs = Int64(ExportOpusEncoder.framesPerPacket) * 1_000_000_000 / 48_000

   232	            try webm.add(
   233	                track: ReelWebM.audio, ptsNs: added * packetNs, key: true,
   234	                discardPaddingNs: padding, data: packet)

   236	        }
   237	        let feed = { (packets: [Data]) throws in
   238	            for packet in packets {
   239	                if let previous = held { try add(previous, 0) }
   240	                held = packet
   241	            }
   242	        }
   243	        var reads = 0
   244	        do {
   245	            while true {
   246	                guard !isStopping else { return }

   248	                try fault?.beforeAudioRead(reads)

   251	                        stopped(with: error)
   252	                        return
   253	                    }

   266	                    method: .roundHalfAwayFromZero
   267	                ).value

   271	                }

   275	            }

   278	            // target is cut whole packets first, then by the last one's DiscardPadding.

   312	        lock.unlock()

   314	        let which = first ? "first" : "later"

   318	    }
   319	
   320	    private static let log = Logger(subsystem: "com.kgalligan.FrameJob", category: "export.webm")
   321

   323	        guard let reader, reader.status == .failed else { return nil }

   326	    }
   327

   337	    /// pump on a stop): the encoder closed, then the file finished off main or dropped and
   338	    /// removed.
   339	    private func allPumpsLeft() {

   342	        let cancelled = cancelRequested
   343	        lock.unlock()

   348	                    + (audioReader.map { "\($0.status.rawValue)" } ?? "none") + shared)
   349	        }

   352	        if cancelled { return finishFailed(Exporter.ExportError.cancelled) }
   353	        guard let webm else { return finishFailed(Exporter.ExportError.cancelled) }

   362	            }

   381	        discard()

   383	    }

   386	    private func discard() {

   389	    }

   392	    private func report(_ result: Result<URL, any Error>) {
   393	        guard let completion else { return }
   394	        self.completion = nil
   395	        completion(result)
   396	    }
   397	}

1	import AVFoundation
     2	
     3	/// The video pump of a row a bundled encoder writes (`settings.writer`, spec §11 CX-12,
     4	/// CX-15): the composed frames converted to I010 on the export's video queue and encoded by
     5	/// SVT-AV1 on a serial encode queue of its own, whose packets go to an `ExportPacketSink` —
     6	/// the `av1` row's passthrough `AVAssetWriterInput` as `av01` samples, or the `av1_webm`
     7	/// row's core writer.
     8	///
     9	/// **Two queues, one owner each.** The video queue reads, converts and hands each frame on,
    10	/// bounded to three in flight (`slots`) so a slow encoder holds the read back; the encode
    11	/// queue owns the encoder and the sink — every `send`, every packet, every append, the
    12	/// flush and the sink's `finish`. Progress is counted by frames SUBMITTED (the encoder's lag
    13	/// is under a second); a cancel is the writer's flag, read before each read, each send and
    14	/// each wait in the sink.
    15	///
    16	/// **The finish** runs once on the encode queue, after every frame queued before it: at the
    17	/// end of a clean read, the end of stream and a drain to the last packet; on a stop (a
    18	/// cancel, a failed read, another pump's failure), the end of stream and a drain that
    19	/// discards; after an encoder error, neither. Every exit finishes the sink and leaves the
    20	/// group exactly once. The encoder itself is torn down by `close()`, after the writer's
    21	/// pumps have all left, as the reader is (G-17).
    22	final class ExportEncodePump {
    23	    /// The settings' `writer` this pump serves.
    24	    static let writer = "svt_av1"
    25	
    26	    let formatDescription: CMVideoFormatDescription
    27	    /// The `av1C` record and the sequence header's colour, and the picture the frames are
    28	    /// (the WebM layout's track, `ExportWebMLayout`).
    29	    let config: ReelAV1.Config
    30	    let picture: ExportAV1Picture
    31	
    32	    private var encoder: SVTAV1Encoder?
    33	    private let converter: ExportI010Converter
    34	    private let encodeQueue = DispatchQueue(
    35	        label: "com.kgalligan.framejob.export.encode", qos: .userInitiated)
    36	    private let range: CMTimeRange
    37	    private let frameDuration: CMTime
    38	    private let slots = DispatchSemaphore(value: 3)
    39	
    40	    // The encode queue's own state.
    41	    private var times: [Int64: CMTime] = [:]
    42	    private var lastTime = CMTime.negativeInfinity
    43	    private var encoderFailed = false
    44	    private var finished = false
    45	
    46	    init(settings: ExportSettings, canvas: CGSize, range: CMTimeRange) throws {
    47	        let frame = ExportWriter.encodedSize(settings)
    48	        let speed = settings.encoderSpeed ?? .balanced
    49	        let rate = settings.videoBitrate.map { max(1, $0) }
    50	            ?? ExportWriter.defaultVideoBitrate(settings, bitsPerPixel: 0.07)
    51	        let picture = ExportAV1Picture(color: settings.color)
    52	        let encoder = try SVTAV1Encoder(
    53	            width: frame.width, height: frame.height, fps: settings.fps, bitsPerSecond: rate,
    54	            speed: speed, picture: picture)
    55	        do {
    56	            config = try ReelAV1.config(sequenceHeader: encoder.sequenceHeader)
    57	        } catch {
    58	            throw Exporter.ExportError.failed(
    59	                "SVT-AV1's sequence header could not be read: \(error.localizedDescription)")
    60	        }
    61	        formatDescription = try ExportAV1Track.formatDescription(
    62	            width: frame.width, height: frame.height, config: config, picture: picture)
    63	        converter = try ExportI010Converter(
    64	            width: frame.width, height: frame.height, canvas: canvas,
    65	            fills: ExportWriter.fillsTheBox(settings, canvas: canvas), picture: picture, pool: 3)
    66	        self.encoder = encoder
    67	        self.picture = picture
    68	        self.range = range
    69	        self.frameDuration = CompositionBuilder.frameDuration(settings.fps)
    70	    }
    71	
    72	    @available(*, unavailable) required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
    73	        fatalError("ExportEncodePump does not support NSCoder")
    74	    }
    75	
    76	    /// Reads `output` to its end on `queue` and encodes it into `sink`; `group` is left once
    77	    /// the sink is finished. `readFailure` answers the reader's error when the read failed;
    78	    /// `fail` records the first failure; `advance` is each submitted frame's file time.
    79	    func run(
    80	        sink: any ExportPacketSink, output: AVAssetReaderOutput, on queue: DispatchQueue,
    81	        group: DispatchGroup, isStopping: @escaping () -> Bool,
    82	        readFailure: @escaping () -> (any Error)?, fail: @escaping (any Error) -> Void,
    83	        advance: @escaping (CMTime) -> Void
    84	    ) {
    85	        group.enter()
    86	        let finish: (Bool) -> Void = { [self] clean in
    87	            encodeQueue.async {
    88	                self.finish(
    89	                    clean: clean, sink: sink, group: group, isStopping: isStopping, fail: fail)
    90	            }
    91	        }
    92	        queue.async { [self] in
    93	            var index: Int64 = 0
    94	            while true {
    95	                guard !isStopping() else { return finish(false) }
    96	                guard let sample = output.copyNextSampleBuffer() else {
    97	                    // Dry: the range is read, or the read failed — never a branded, done
    98	                    // file after a failed read.
    99	                    if let error = readFailure() {
   100	                        fail(error)
   101	                        return finish(false)
   102	                    }
   103	                    return finish(true)
   104	                }
   105	                let time = CMSampleBufferGetPresentationTimeStamp(sample) - range.start
   106	                guard time.isNumeric, time >= .zero else { continue }
   107	                slots.wait()
   108	                guard let pixels = CMSampleBufferGetImageBuffer(sample),
   109	                    let frame = converter.convert(pixels)
   110	                else {
   111	                    slots.signal()
   112	                    fail(Exporter.ExportError.failed(
   113	                        "A frame could not be prepared for the encoder."))
   114	                    return finish(false)
   115	                }
   116	                let at = index
   117	                index += 1
   118	                encodeQueue.async {
   119	                    self.encode(
   120	                        frame, index: at, time: time, sink: sink, isStopping: isStopping,
   121	                        fail: fail)
   122	                }
   123	                advance(time)
   124	            }
   125	        }
   126	    }
   127	
   128	    /// The encoder's teardown, on the encode queue, once every input is finished.
   129	    func close() {
   130	        encodeQueue.async { [self] in encoder = nil }
   131	    }
   132	
   133	    // MARK: - The encode queue
   134	
   135	    private func encode(
   136	        _ frame: I010Frame, index: Int64, time: CMTime, sink: any ExportPacketSink,
   137	        isStopping: () -> Bool, fail: (any Error) -> Void
   138	    ) {
   139	        defer {
   140	            converter.recycle(frame)
   141	            slots.signal()
   142	        }
   143	        guard !finished, !encoderFailed, !isStopping(), let encoder else { return }
   144	        do {
   145	            try encoder.send(frame, index: index)
   146	            times[index] = time
   147	            while let packet = try encoder.nextPacket(wait: false) {
   148	                guard write(packet, sink: sink, isStopping: isStopping, fail: fail) else {
   149	                    return
   150	                }
   151	            }
   152	        } catch {
   153	            encoderFailed = true
   154	            fail(error)
   155	        }
   156	    }
   157	
   158	    /// One packet into the file: false once the export cannot go on.
   159	    private func write(
   160	        _ packet: SVTAV1Encoder.Packet, sink: any ExportPacketSink, isStopping: () -> Bool,
   161	        fail: (any Error) -> Void
   162	    ) -> Bool {
   163	        guard !packet.data.isEmpty else { return true }
   164	        var data = packet.data
   165	        guard ReelAV1.stripTemporalDelimiters(&data) else {
   166	            fail(Exporter.ExportError.failed("SVT-AV1 wrote a packet the core could not read."))
   167	            return false
   168	        }
   169	        guard let time = times.removeValue(forKey: packet.pts), time > lastTime else {
   170	            fail(Exporter.ExportError.failed("SVT-AV1 wrote a frame out of order."))
   171	            return false
   172	        }
   173	        lastTime = time
   174	        if let error = sink.append(
   175	            data, at: time, duration: frameDuration, key: packet.isKey, isStopping: isStopping)
   176	        {
   177	            if !(error is ExportPacketSinkStopped) { fail(error) }
   178	            return false
   179	        }
   180	        return true
   181	    }
   182	
   183	    /// The one exit: the end of stream and the drain as `clean` and the encoder allow, then
   184	    /// the sink finished and the group left, exactly once.
   185	    private func finish(
   186	        clean: Bool, sink: any ExportPacketSink, group: DispatchGroup, isStopping: () -> Bool,
   187	        fail: (any Error) -> Void
   188	    ) {
   189	        guard !finished else { return }
   190	        finished = true
   191	        defer {
   192	            sink.finish()
   193	            group.leave()
   194	        }
   195	        guard !encoderFailed, let encoder else { return }
   196	        do {
   197	            try encoder.sendEndOfStream()
   198	            var writing = clean && !isStopping()
   199	            while let packet = try encoder.nextPacket(wait: true) {
   200	                if writing {
   201	                    writing = write(packet, sink: sink, isStopping: isStopping, fail: fail)
   202	                }
   203	                if packet.isLast { break }
   204	            }
   205	        } catch {
   206	            encoderFailed = true
   207	            if clean { fail(error) }
   208	        }
   209	    }
   210	}

def long_doc(instance, name):
    """W9's project: AV.mov 24 times on a 1080p canvas at scale 3."""
    doc = av1.Doc(instance, name, 1920, 1080)
    media = doc.media(av1.AV)
    track = doc.track()
    for k in range(24):
        doc.call("add_clip", track=track, media=media, at=k * 5 * SEC)
    clips = [c["id"] for c in doc.call("get_project")["project"]["clips"]]
    doc.call("set_video", clips=clips, patch={"scale": 3.0})
    return doc


def row_fault(ident, app, logs):
    spec, want = FAULTS[ident]
    instance = av1.Instance(f"fault-{ident.lower()}", app,
                            arguments=["-RCDevWebMFault", spec])
    logs.append(instance)
    out = WORK / "out"
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = out / f"{ident.lower()}.webm"
    path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    doc, ok, detail = None, False, ""
    marker = "is held" if ident == "F3" else "framejob webm dev fault:"

    def log_lines():
        try:
            return instance.log.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()
        except OSError:
            return []
    try:
        if instance.client is None:
            raise RuntimeError(f"the app did not listen ({instance.log})")
        doc = long_doc(instance, ident.lower())
        job = doc.client.call_with("export", {"project": doc.path, "path": str(path),
                                              "preset": "av1_webm"})["export_id"]
        deadline, fired = time.monotonic() + 300, None
        status = {}
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            if any(marker in line for line in log_lines()):
                fired = time.monotonic()
                break
            status = doc.client.call("export_status", export_id=job)
            if status.get("status") in ("done", "failed", "cancelled"):
                break
            time.sleep(0.05)
        if fired is None:
            raise RuntimeError(f"the fault never fired: {status}")
        if ident == "F3":
            doc.client.call("cancel_export", export_id=job)
        final = {}
        while time.monotonic() - fired < 120:
            final = doc.client.call("export_status", export_id=job)
            if final.get("status") in ("done", "failed", "cancelled"):
                break
            time.sleep(0.05)
        took = time.monotonic() - fired
        time.sleep(0.5)    # the readers' line follows the pumps, on main
        readers = [line.split("readers: ", 1)[1] for line in log_lines() if "readers: " in line]
        exists = path.exists()
        named = want == "cancelled" or "dev fault" in json.dumps(final)
        ok = (final.get("status") == want and named and took <= FAULT_BOUND and not exists
              and readers == ["video 4, audio 4"])
        detail = (f"{spec}: status {final.get('status')!r} (want {want!r}) {took:.2f} s after "
                  f"the {'cancel' if ident == 'F3' else 'fault'} (≤ {FAULT_BOUND}); the dev "
                  f"fault named: {named}; readers {readers} (want ['video 4, audio 4'], 4 = "
                  f"cancelled); a file at the path: {exists}; {json.dumps(final)[:300]}")
    except (mcp.ToolError, KeyError, RuntimeError, OSError) as error:
        detail = f"{spec}: {type(error).__name__}: {error}"
    finally:
        if doc is not None:
            try:
                doc.close()
            except Exception:  # an instance that died is the row's FAIL already
                pass
        instance.stop()
    check(ident, ok, detail)


def run_fault_rows(app, logs):
    for ident in FAULTS:
        row_fault(ident, app, logs)


def run_w_rows(app, logs):
    out = WORK / "out"
    av1.tree_copy.remove_tree(str(out))
    out.mkdir(parents=True)
    instance = av1.Instance("w", app)
    logs.append(instance)
    idents = [r for r in ROWS if r.startswith("W")]
    try:
        if instance.client is None:
            for ident in idents:
                check(ident, False, f"the app did not listen ({instance.log})")
            return
        doc = hlg = None
        try:
            doc = a1_doc(instance, "w1")
            w1 = rows_w1_w5(doc, out)
            row_w6(doc, out)
            doc.call("set_range", start=0, end=5 * SEC)
            row_w7(doc, out)
            if w1 is not None:
                row_w10_w11(doc, out, w1)
                row_w12(instance, w1)
            else:
                for ident in ("W10", "W11"):
                    check(ident, False, "W1's file is missing")
            hlg = a1_doc(instance, "w8", hlg=True)
            row_w8(hlg, out)
        except (mcp.ToolError, KeyError, IndexError) as error:
            for ident in idents:
                if ident not in results:
                    check(ident, False, f"A1's project could not be made: {error}")
        finally:
            for d in (doc, hlg):
                if d is not None:
                    d.close()
        row_w13(instance, out)
        row_w9(instance, out)
    finally:
        instance.stop()

def run_probe(sources):
    """P1–P5 and A1–A5: `webm_audio_probe.swift` built over `sources` and run."""
    import reference_build
    import swift_build
    out = WORK / ("probe" if Path(sources).resolve() == (ROOT / SOURCES).resolve()
                  else "probe-mutant")
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    entry = out / "main.swift"
    text = PROBE_SWIFT.read_text()
    if not entry.exists() or entry.read_text() != text:
        entry.write_text(text)
    binary, answer = out / "webm-audio-probe", out / "answer.json"
    defines = reference_build.tree_defines(Path(sources).parent.parent, ["FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS"])
    try:
        built = swift_build.build(sources=swift_build.app_sources(sources) + [entry],
                                  output=binary, defines=defines)
        if not built.reused:
            print(f"probe built in {built.seconds:.0f} s", flush=True)
    except swift_build.SwiftBuildFailed as error:
        lines = [line for line in error.diagnostics if ": error:" in line]
        for ident in PROBE_ROWS:
            check(ident, False, "the probe did not build: "
                  + " | ".join(lines[:3] or list(error.diagnostics[:3]) or [str(error)]))
        return
    answer.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    ran = bounded.run([str(binary), str(answer)], 120)
    if ran["expired"] or ran["rc"] != 0 or not answer.exists():
        for ident in PROBE_ROWS:
            check(ident, False, "the probe did not run: "
                  + (ran["stdout"] + ran["stderr"]).strip()[-300:])
        return
    answered = {r["name"].split(" ")[0]: r for r in json.loads(answer.read_text())["rows"]}
    for ident in PROBE_ROWS:
        row = answered.get(ident)
        if row is None:
            check(ident, False, "the probe answered no such row")
        else:
            check(ident, row["ok"], f"{row['name'][len(ident) + 1:]}: {row['detail']}")


def run_readers_probe(sources=ROOT / SOURCES):
    """R1: `webm_readers_probe.swift` beside the tree's two export shaders as
    `default.metallib`, `Blank.mp4`, `Silence.caf` and the fonts, run over AV.mov."""
    import shutil
    import reference_build
    import swift_build
    folder = WORK / "readers-probe"
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    entry = folder / "main.swift"
    text = READERS_SWIFT.read_text()
    if not entry.exists() or entry.read_text() != text:
        entry.write_text(text)
    resources = Path(sources).parent / "Resources"
    for name in ("Blank.mp4", "Silence.caf"):
        shutil.copy2(resources / name, folder / name)
    if (resources / "Fonts").is_dir():
        shutil.copytree(resources / "Fonts", folder / "Fonts", dirs_exist_ok=True)
    airs = []
    for shader in ("Compositor", "ExportI010"):
        air = folder / f"{shader}.air"
        step = run(["xcrun", "-sdk", "macosx", "metal", "-c",
                    resources / "Shaders" / f"{shader}.metal", "-o", air], 300)
        if step["rc"] != 0:
            return check("R1", False, f"{shader}.metal did not build: {step['stderr'][-300:]}")
        airs.append(air)
    step = run(["xcrun", "-sdk", "macosx", "metallib", *airs, "-o", folder / "default.metallib"],
               300)
    if step["rc"] != 0:
        return check("R1", False, f"the metallib did not build: {step['stderr'][-300:]}")
    binary, answer = folder / "webm-readers-probe", folder / "answer.json"
    try:
        defines = reference_build.tree_defines(Path(sources).parent.parent,
                                               ["FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS"])
        swift_build.build(sources=swift_build.app_sources(sources) + [entry], output=binary,
                          defines=defines)
    except swift_build.SwiftBuildFailed as error:
        lines = [line for line in error.diagnostics if ": error:" in line]
        return check("R1", False, "the probe did not build: "
                     + " | ".join(lines[:3] or list(error.diagnostics[:3]) or [str(error)]))
    answer.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    ran = bounded.run([str(binary), str(av1.AV), str(answer)], 600, cwd=str(folder))
    if ran["expired"] or ran["rc"] != 0 or not answer.exists():
        return check("R1", False, "the probe did not run: "
                     + (ran["stdout"] + ran["stderr"]).strip()[-300:])
    row = json.loads(answer.read_text())["rows"][0]
    check("R1", row["ok"], f"{row['name'][3:]}: {row['detail']}")


def run_probe_mutant(name):
    """A probe mutant: `app/Sources` copied with the anchor replaced, the probe alone."""
    import shutil
    mutant = MUTANTS[name]
    copy = WORK / "mutant-probe"
    shutil.rmtree(copy, ignore_errors=True)
    sources = copy / "app" / "Sources"
    shutil.copytree(ROOT / SOURCES, sources)
    for path, anchor, replacement in mutant["anchors"]:
        target = copy / path
        text = target.read_text()
        if text.count(anchor) != 1:
            print(f"mutant {name}: the control could not be performed — the anchor occurs "
                  f"{text.count(anchor)} times in {path}")
            return 2
        target.write_text(text.replace(anchor, replacement))
    try:
        run_probe(sources)
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(copy, ignore_errors=True)
    failing = sorted(k for k, v in results.items() if not v)
    named = sorted(mutant["rows"])
    print(f"mutant {name}: named {named}, failing {failing}")
    if any(results.get(r) is None for r in PROBE_ROWS) or (
            failing == PROBE_ROWS and named != PROBE_ROWS):
        print(f"mutant {name}: the control could not be performed — the probe failed whole")

def long_doc(instance, name):
    """W9's project: AV.mov 24 times on a 1080p canvas at scale 3."""
    doc = av1.Doc(instance, name, 1920, 1080)
    media = doc.media(av1.AV)
    track = doc.track()
    for k in range(24):
        doc.call("add_clip", track=track, media=media, at=k * 5 * SEC)
    clips = [c["id"] for c in doc.call("get_project")["project"]["clips"]]
    doc.call("set_video", clips=clips, patch={"scale": 3.0})
    return doc


def row_fault(ident, app, logs):
    spec, want = FAULTS[ident]
    instance = av1.Instance(f"fault-{ident.lower()}", app,
                            arguments=["-RCDevWebMFault", spec])
    logs.append(instance)
    out = WORK / "out"
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = out / f"{ident.lower()}.webm"
    path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    doc, ok, detail = None, False, ""
    marker = "is held" if ident == "F3" else "framejob webm dev fault:"

    def log_lines():
        try:
            return instance.log.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()
        except OSError:
            return []
    try:
        if instance.client is None:
            raise RuntimeError(f"the app did not listen ({instance.log})")
        doc = long_doc(instance, ident.lower())
        job = doc.client.call_with("export", {"project": doc.path, "path": str(path),
                                              "preset": "av1_webm"})["export_id"]
        deadline, fired = time.monotonic() + 300, None
        status = {}
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            if any(marker in line for line in log_lines()):
                fired = time.monotonic()
                break
            status = doc.client.call("export_status", export_id=job)
            if status.get("status") in ("done", "failed", "cancelled"):
                break
            time.sleep(0.05)
        if fired is None:
            raise RuntimeError(f"the fault never fired: {status}")
        if ident == "F3":
            doc.client.call("cancel_export", export_id=job)
        final = {}
        while time.monotonic() - fired < 120:
            final = doc.client.call("export_status", export_id=job)
            if final.get("status") in ("done", "failed", "cancelled"):
                break
            time.sleep(0.05)
        took = time.monotonic() - fired
        time.sleep(0.5)    # the readers' line follows the pumps, on main
        readers = [line.split("readers: ", 1)[1] for line in log_lines() if "readers: " in line]
        exists = path.exists()
        named = want == "cancelled" or "dev fault" in json.dumps(final)
        ok = (final.get("status") == want and named and took <= FAULT_BOUND and not exists
              and readers == ["video 4, audio 4"])
        detail = (f"{spec}: status {final.get('status')!r} (want {want!r}) {took:.2f} s after "
                  f"the {'cancel' if ident == 'F3' else 'fault'} (≤ {FAULT_BOUND}); the dev "
                  f"fault named: {named}; readers {readers} (want ['video 4, audio 4'], 4 = "
                  f"cancelled); a file at the path: {exists}; {json.dumps(final)[:300]}")
    except (mcp.ToolError, KeyError, RuntimeError, OSError) as error:
        detail = f"{spec}: {type(error).__name__}: {error}"
    finally:
        if doc is not None:
            try:
                doc.close()
            except Exception:  # an instance that died is the row's FAIL already
                pass
        instance.stop()
    check(ident, ok, detail)

def run_probe(sources):
    """P1–P5 and A1–A5: `webm_audio_probe.swift` built over `sources` and run."""
    import reference_build
    import swift_build
    out = WORK / ("probe" if Path(sources).resolve() == (ROOT / SOURCES).resolve()
                  else "probe-mutant")
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    entry = out / "main.swift"
    text = PROBE_SWIFT.read_text()
    if not entry.exists() or entry.read_text() != text:
        entry.write_text(text)
    binary, answer = out / "webm-audio-probe", out / "answer.json"
    defines = reference_build.tree_defines(Path(sources).parent.parent, ["FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS"])
    try:
        built = swift_build.build(sources=swift_build.app_sources(sources) + [entry],
                                  output=binary, defines=defines)
        if not built.reused:
            print(f"probe built in {built.seconds:.0f} s", flush=True)
    except swift_build.SwiftBuildFailed as error:
        lines = [line for line in error.diagnostics if ": error:" in line]
        for ident in PROBE_ROWS:
            check(ident, False, "the probe did not build: "
                  + " | ".join(lines[:3] or list(error.diagnostics[:3]) or [str(error)]))
        return
    answer.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    ran = bounded.run([str(binary), str(answer)], 120)
    if ran["expired"] or ran["rc"] != 0 or not answer.exists():
        for ident in PROBE_ROWS:
            check(ident, False, "the probe did not run: "
                  + (ran["stdout"] + ran["stderr"]).strip()[-300:])
        return
    answered = {r["name"].split(" ")[0]: r for r in json.loads(answer.read_text())["rows"]}
    for ident in PROBE_ROWS:
        row = answered.get(ident)
        if row is None:
            check(ident, False, "the probe answered no such row")
        else:
            check(ident, row["ok"], f"{row['name'][len(ident) + 1:]}: {row['detail']}")


def run_readers_probe(sources=ROOT / SOURCES):
    """R1: `webm_readers_probe.swift` beside the tree's two export shaders as
    `default.metallib`, `Blank.mp4`, `Silence.caf` and the fonts, run over AV.mov."""
    import shutil
    import reference_build
    import swift_build

    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    entry = folder / "main.swift"
    text = READERS_SWIFT.read_text()
    if not entry.exists() or entry.read_text() != text:
        entry.write_text(text)
    resources = Path(sources).parent / "Resources"
    for name in ("Blank.mp4", "Silence.caf"):

    if (resources / "Fonts").is_dir():
        shutil.copytree(resources / "Fonts", folder / "Fonts", dirs_exist_ok=True)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Issue batch B1, against the built app: the export gate follows nests at
any depth (#73), `import_media` waits as long as an ffmpeg conversion may
legitimately run (#67), and an export's Cancel during the loudness
measurement only sets a flag — the measurement's own loop cancels its reader
(#74, spec §11 G-17).

One owned instance on a scratch socket (`mcp.scratch_socket`), launched with
`-ApplePersistenceIgnoreState YES
-RCFFmpegImport always -RCFFmpegPath <work>/standin/ffmpeg`, stopped by PID,
its log at `tools/proof/work/export-cancel/framejob.log`; nothing else
is ever killed. **The instance runs in a scratch home** (issue batch B82,
#236): `CFFIXED_USER_HOME=<work>/home`, made bare, so the `Rewrapped/` I1's
conversion lands in is `<work>/home/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/
Rewrapped/`; the gate, import and cancel groups all use that one instance.
The M rows' probe (`export_cancel_probe`) keeps the caller's environment.
Nothing outside `tools/proof/work/` and the scratch socket's own temporary
folder (`mcp.scratch_socket`, removed when the instance stops) is written,
except the app's and the probe's own `UserDefaults` domains, which that
batch does not move.
Every child runs under `graphics_spike/bounded.py`. The M rows
run `export_cancel_probe.swift`, an in-process instrument built like
`graphics_proof.py`'s pin probe into `tools/proof/work/export-cancel-probe/`
(through `swift_build.py`, reused when every input is byte-identical to a
cached build's; the line reads `probe: built …` or `probe: up to date …`); a
probe that will not build scores M0–M2 as FAILURES.

G1  (CONTROL) `new_project`; `write_graphic gate` (compiles, 30 frames, one
    rect); `add_graphic_clip gate` at 0; `nest` it; `add_text_clip` right
    after the nest clip; `nest` both. `get_project`: timeline nest clip →
    nest B holding a nest clip → nest A holding the `gate` clip. `export
    h264` succeeds and the file exists.
G2  `write_graphic gate` with a syntax error answers `ok: false`; a sentinel
    file at the path; `export h264` to it is an error starting "The export
    was not started:" naming "gate", and the sentinel's bytes are unchanged.
I1  stand-in `ffprobe` (fixed JSON: one h264 640×360 30/1 stream, 10 s) and
    `ffmpeg` (sleeps 45 s, copies `media/A.mov` to its last argument, then
    touches `standin/ffmpeg.exited`); `import_media` of a 4096-byte
    `slow-<hex>.mkv` answers ok after ≥ 45 s, kind video, 640×360, a `.mov`
    directly inside the scratch home's Rewrapped. When
    `<work>/home/Library/Application Support` is not a directory the scratch
    home did not take: I1 FAILS and no import is made. Cleanup, whatever it
    answered and before the
    instance stops: wait for `ffmpeg.exited` (120 s from the call's start),
    then for no `slow-<hex>-*.partial.mov` (10 s), then delete every
    Rewrapped entry starting `slow-<hex>-` (parent-checked) and the fixture.
    An expired bound fails the row and names the leftovers.
M0  (CONTROL) a 60 s noise WAV (`NOISE_SECONDS`, 300 before issue batch
    B13) imported over MCP onto four tracks with `noise_reduction: 1.0`,
    saved; the probe's uncancelled run is `success` with a measurement
    `window` ≥ `WINDOW_FLOOR` (8.0 s).
M1  `--runs` probe runs, each cancelling `delay` s (uniform in
    [0.2, window/2]) into the measurement: every run rc 0 (a signal or an
    expiry is a crash), `phase_at_cancel` "Measuring loudness…", `outcome`
    `cancelled`, `left` false. Prints the crash count.
M2  every M1 `latency` ≤ `LATENCY_BOUND` (2.0 s; 1.0 s before B13, when two
    full runs printed 0.889 s and 0.790 s).
Z1  `grep "Frame Job: "` over this launch's log prints nothing.

I found nothing to object to with evidence, so the objections file has no objections and ends `verdict: proceed`.

Written to /Users/kevingalligan/.claude/litecode/framejob/g17-mp4/02-objections.md, from the worktree /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob-lane-b at e759112.

What I checked:
- **The video pump's own cancel:** every exit from the plain pump in `app/Sources/ExporterWriter.swift` goes through its `stop` closure. So the cancel placed there always comes after that pump's last read, on its own queue. A clean export never cancels a reader, because nothing is stopping it.
- **The av1 row's cancel block:** in `app/Sources/ExportEncodePump.swift`, `run`'s whole read loop is one `queue.async` block on `videoQueue`. A cancel block queued right after `run(…)` therefore runs only after the last read, as it does in `ExportWebMWriter.swift`.
- **The three mutants:** each one fails exactly its named F rows through the readers line:
  - `shared-reader` shows "(one reader)" on F1–F4.
  - `no-own-cancel` leaves the readers reading (status 1) on F1–F4.
  - `encode-cancel-dropped` leaves video at status 1 on F4 only, since F1–F3 are `h264` and never use the encode pump.
- **The anchors:** all three compile once replaced. Swift reads `??` before `&&`, so `self?.isStopping ?? true && false` is valid. The only proof anchor that points into `ExporterWriter.swift` is `av1_export_proof.py:198`. No probe builds an `ExportWriter` or reads its `reader`, and the only place that creates one is `ExporterImageSequence.swift:110`.
- **The fault helper and the proof refactor:**
  - Splitting `ExportWebMDevFault` into `word` and `note` keeps WebM's log lines byte-identical.
  - The `fault_row` and `readers_rows` changes fit the current `row_fault` and `run_readers_probe` code in `webm_export_proof.py`.
  - The C2 expectation (`text_doc`: one stream, "audio none") matches what WebM's W13 already sees.
- **Size:** moving the audio half out takes about 55 lines off, which leaves room under the 600-line cap.

One weakness I did not raise as an objection, because it copies the accepted C3 design: `shared-reader` is caught only because the readers line reports `===`. No row ever shows a shared reader actually starving under `ExportWriter`.
